title: Data Engineer
summary: Data engineers build the pipelines that move data from apps and files into warehouses where analysts and data scientists can use it. It suits students who enjoy programming, databases and making systems reliable.

nodes.title: Python programming
nodes.summary: Learn Python well: functions, data structures, files, error handling and modules. Most pipeline code, scripts and tools in data engineering are written in Python.
nodes.proof: A script that reads a CSV or JSON file, validates and cleans it, and writes the result to a new file, pushed to GitHub.

nodes.title: SQL and data modelling
nodes.summary: Go beyond SELECT: joins, window functions, indexes, normalisation and designing tables. Strong SQL is the core skill interviewers test for data engineering roles.

resources.title: CS50's Introduction to Databases with SQL – Harvard

nodes.proof: A small database schema you designed (for example, a college library) with sample data and 15 queries including window functions.

nodes.title: Docker and containers
nodes.summary: Learn to run databases and tools in containers, write a Dockerfile and use Docker Compose. Containers let you run a whole pipeline on your laptop the same way it runs elsewhere.
nodes.proof: A Docker Compose file that starts a database and your Python ingestion script together with one command.

nodes.title: Batch pipelines and orchestration
nodes.summary: Learn how to extract, transform and load data on a schedule, and how an orchestrator like Apache Airflow runs tasks as a DAG with retries and dependencies.

resources.title: Airflow 101: Building Your First Workflow – Apache Airflow

nodes.proof: An Airflow DAG that downloads a public dataset daily, cleans it and loads it into a database, with a screenshot of successful runs.

nodes.title: Data warehouses and dbt
nodes.summary: Learn how analytical warehouses differ from app databases, and use dbt to turn raw tables into clean, tested models with SQL. DuckDB lets you practise this for free on a laptop.

resources.title: Quickstart for dbt Core using DuckDB

nodes.proof: A dbt project with staging and final models, tests on key columns and generated documentation.

nodes.title: Big data processing with Spark
nodes.summary: Learn PySpark DataFrames: reading files, filtering, joining and grouping data that is too large for pandas, and how lazy evaluation works.
nodes.proof: A PySpark job that processes a multi-file public dataset and writes aggregated results as Parquet files.

nodes.title: Streaming basics with Kafka
nodes.summary: Understand topics, producers and consumers, and run Kafka locally. Learn this after batch pipelines; many entry-level roles focus on batch work first.
nodes.proof: A small producer that sends events to a Kafka topic and a consumer that writes them to a database.

nodes.title: End-to-end pipeline project
nodes.summary: Build one pipeline from a real public source to a trusted, documented output: ingest, store, transform with dbt or Spark, schedule it and add data quality checks. This is your main interview talking point.
nodes.proof: A GitHub repo with an architecture diagram, setup steps that work on a fresh machine and a dashboard or table built from the pipeline.

nodes.title: Interview preparation and applying
nodes.summary: Practise SQL query questions, Python coding questions and basic system design (how data flows, partitioning, queues). Be ready to explain every choice in your capstone pipeline.

resources.title: 30 SQL Queries Interview Questions and Answers – roadmap.sh
Top 30 System Design Interview Questions – roadmap.sh

nodes.proof: Solve the roadmap.sh SQL and Python question sets without notes, and explain your capstone design to a friend in 5 minutes.

sources.title: 30 SQL Queries Interview Questions and Answers – roadmap.sh
